app.title: JalRakshak 360
app.summary: A person narrows a set of monitored locations by district and risk level, then sees headline counts, a map with markers coloured by risk level, and a queue of locations ranked by their combined risk score. They open one location to see a bar chart of its five risk factors, the top three reasons it was flagged, and a list of recommended actions with priorities. A slider changes one input, rainfall, for a chosen location and shows how the rule-based score and level would change. Lower panels show the supporting sources and their data-quality status: reported contamination indicators by district and parameter, how close and how recent the nearest monitoring station is for each location, flagged sensor jumps, and census population context.

task.text: Decide which locations need water-quality intervention first, using a composite risk score whose factors are explained, with a recommended action for each location.

data.text: A table of monitored locations with coordinates and risk indicators. Each location has computed factor scores, an anomaly score, a fused risk score, a level and a priority. Beside it are district-level tables of reported contamination counts per parameter, station-level audits of sensor telemetry, and census population context.
data.item: a monitored location (a village water point) with coordinates, risk-factor scores and an assigned priority

stage.text: prioritising locations for intervention after risk scoring, before field testing and inspection

mechanism.text: Sidebar filters drive the headline counts, the risk-coloured map and the ranked priority table together. Choosing a location in a selectbox opens its factor breakdown and rule-based recommended actions. A separate slider reruns the rule-based score for one location under changed rainfall. Further down, static panels summarise each data source and flag its quality issues.

field.text: composite risk scoring for drinking-water quality and intervention prioritisation in environmental engineering

workflow.name: rank locations by a composite risk score and choose where to act

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Sidebar selectboxes restrict the locations to one district and/or one risk level (CRITICAL, HIGH, WATCH, LOW).

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Headline counts (locations, critical, high, P1, population covered) and a map with each location marked in its risk-level colour, plus popups showing score, priority and anomaly score.

steps.step: rank items by a computed score
steps.here: The intervention priority queue lists the filtered locations sorted by final risk score, with level, priority and AI anomaly score.

Choosing a location shows its score, level, priority and anomaly score. A bar chart shows its five risk factors, the top three factors are listed as 'why was this flagged', and rule-based recommended actions are listed with P1/P2/P3 priorities.

steps.step: recompute a value under a changed input
steps.here: For a chosen location, a slider changes 7-day rainfall from -50% to +100%. The rule-based score and level are recomputed and shown with the change from the original score.

steps.step: check the supporting sources and their quality
steps.here: Panels summarise district contamination indicators by parameter and show which stations are near or stale, which telemetry jumps are flagged, the census population context, and the inclusion status of each source.

distinctive: The final score is a weighted sum of five factor scores fused with a machine-learned anomaly score, and each location's top factors are listed as the reason it was flagged.
A rule table turns each location's risk level and factor thresholds into recommended actions with P1–P3 priorities.
A what-if slider perturbs one environmental driver (rainfall) and recomputes only the explainable rule-based score, not the anomaly model.

Each data source carries an explicit status saying whether it feeds the score (for example monitoring-only, or not merged because the regions differ), with distance, freshness and sign-convention review flags for nearby sensor stations.

parts.title: Filters
parts.summary: Selectboxes in the sidebar narrow the locations to one district and one risk level, and every view above the simulator uses the result.

parts.title: Headline counts
parts.summary: Shows how many locations are monitored, how many are critical or high, how many are P1 interventions and the total population covered.

parts.title: Water Risk Map
parts.summary: Places each filtered location on a map as a marker coloured by risk level. Its popup shows the score, priority and anomaly score.

parts.title: Intervention Priority Queue
parts.summary: A table of the filtered locations ranked by final risk score, showing level, priority and AI anomaly score.

parts.title: What-If Rainfall Simulator
parts.summary: Lets the person pick a location and change its rainfall by a percentage, then shows the recomputed rule-based score and level next to the original values.

parts.title: Location Intelligence
parts.summary: For one chosen location, shows its score, level, priority and anomaly score, a bar chart of its five risk factors, its top three factors, and recommended actions with priorities.

parts.title: Verified Government Water-Quality Intelligence
parts.summary: Summarises reported contamination indicators across districts with counts and a top-10 table. A chosen district's non-zero indicators are shown as a bar chart by parameter.

parts.title: Source coverage and data-quality status
parts.summary: Tables and counts show the nearest groundwater station for each location with distance, freshness and sign-review flags. They also show stations with large telemetry jumps, census population context, and whether each source is included in the risk score.
